name: YOOPAI Silk PLA @Creality CR-10 Smart
filament_notes:
YOOPAI manufacturer data, generated by scripts/shop_profiles/gen_filaments.py.
Dry 55 C for 8 h.
Manufacturer max speed 200 mm/s.
Max volumetric speed 10 mm3/s matches the manufacturer's rating for this printer.
Temperature set for ~40 mm/s on this printer: 210 C (first layer 210 C). Manufacturer bands: 190-215 C at 50-150 mm/s; 215-230 C at 150-250 mm/s. Printing much faster or slower than this printer's default process? Adjust the nozzle temperature along those bands.
MAJOR CONFLICT between YOOPAI sources. yoopai.com only sells this as 250g Silk PLA starter bundles (8/16 rolls); those pages give no settings in text but carry the lineup comparison chart image, PLA Silk row: 210-240C, <200 mm/s, 55C 8h. Per the source-preference rule those yoopai.com values are recorded for nozzle/speed/drying. The Amazon 1kg single-colour listings (Silver B0GTTM2977, Gold, Copper, DarkGold, RougeRed etc.), the 2kg twin packs and the Amazon 250g x8 bundle (B0GTTM396W) all say 'Recommended settings: nozzle 190-215C, bed 30-60C, speed 50-80 mm/s; slower speeds improve the silk finish'. Bed 30-60C is taken from Amazon because yoopai.com publishes no bed temperature for silk. The Amazon 1kg image gallery adds a speed/temperature table (190-215C @50-150 mm/s, 215-230C @150-250 mm/s), recorded as speed_temp_bands; note that it exceeds both the chart (<200) and the bullet text (50-80). A shop wanting the conservative Amazon text values should use 190-215C / 80 mm/s. Spool shows the Ingeo logo. 1.75 +/-0.03 mm. Silk text structure ('Neatly Wound', 'slower speeds ... silk finish') resembles SUNLU's Silk PLA+ listing, but the numbers differ from SUNLU's (205-215C, bed 60-80C, 30-60 mm/s).
Source: https://www.yoopai.com/products/yoopai-pla-silk-filament-1-75mm-250g-starter-bundle-8-rolls
